svg.aria-label: How E2B spawns a sandbox. Once, when the template is built, it boots the template, snapshots it and records which memory pages fault in, and stores a snapfile, memory layers, rootfs layers and metadata. Every spawn then resumes that snapshot instead of keeping a warm pool. Firecracker starts in a network namespace without the jailer, userfaultfd pages memory back in with the hot pages first, the rootfs comes over NBD and the VM resumes, MMDS gets only a hash of the access token, and envd inside the guest gets the real token, which lives in guest RAM and never in the snapshot files.
svg.text: once, when the template is built
memory paged back in on demand
only a hash sits in MMDS
the real token lives in guest RAM,
